CHAPTER IV
MITIGATING MEASURES INCLUDED IN THE PROPOSED ACTION
GENERAL ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROLS AND LEGISLATION
Planning for Development; Organizations and Structures
The most essential process in the orderly growth of any rapidly expanding community is the effective implementation of land use and development planning and control programs.
The success of these programs is dependent in part on the organ-\nizations which are charged with their implementation and in part on the
support given them by their constituents and other entities with power
over the situation.
The following quotation expressed the opinion that local planners would be overwhelmed:
"It concerns us that in no cases is there any record of any sudden and rapid industrialization occurring in any area (much less a rural one) being adequately controlled and regulated through existing governmental structures. In case after case the existing literature reflects that local communities and their social and governmental structures are overwhelmed and thrown into a chaotic and confusing situation that paralyzes them. Meanwhile, development marches on."
Northern Cheyenne Research Project
The Big Horn County Planning Board and the Big Horn Area Planning Organization have or are acquiring the basic tools with which they can effectively bring about land use control programs. These include the subdivision ordinance which, with its self-policing principle, demands that a developer's plans and operations meet the minimum standards for good community planning, or his plat will not be recorded.
